decisions.reason: After several years the standalone address-autocomplete service is likely to have revealed limited differentiated value versus generic alternatives, so its option value is low relative to the firm's more strategic energy-market offerings.

The Austrian gas grid fee database fits the firm's data capabilities but serves a relatively narrow adjacent market and likely carries ongoing update costs, so management would probably reallocate resources once initial learning has occurred.
This service is close to the firm's regulated-process core, likely inexpensive to maintain once built, and still has meaningful upside as part of the firm's broader analytics and compliance platform.
An end-customer tariff database with several models supports the firm's platform direction and customer workflows, so despite maintenance effort it remains a valuable option worth keeping open.
Custom web services reinforce client relationships and the firm's end-to-end digitization strategy, making them a flexible low-regret offering to retain.
A standalone postal-code lookup service appears generic and weakly differentiated for this specialized firm, so after the trial period management would likely discontinue it as a marketed product.
